content.comment_body: I'm teaching students about industrial automation and PLC programming. I use [product_name] demo software for writing programs and running simulations. I've noticed conversion errors when switching between FBD and LAD diagram types. 1) Are these conversion issues documented? 2) I'm currently using [version_no] from August 2014. Is this the latest version available? Thanks for any information. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. This is a user-driven space, so for official statements from [company_name], you'll need to submit a Support Request. Regarding point 1: I mostly work with FBD, so I'm not able to comment on specific LAD-to-FBD conversion errors. Regarding point 2: The latest demo is [version_no], while the licensed software is up to [version_no].

Do you have examples of errors when converting between LAD and FBD? Usually, both formats have their strengths, so conversion may not always be necessary. I've programmed in LAD recently without issues, though years ago some errors existed. Unfortunately, there's no comprehensive list of these known errors. Regards, [user_name]

This is a longstanding issue in the [product_name] [version_no] software. Errors used to occur when connections between blocks broke. Loading the program in the latest version [version_no] and converting to LAD resolved these issues.
Hi [user_name], The program was designed in FBD and is attached. After converting to LAD, the simulation produces different results.
Here's the converted program. FBD diagram converted to LAD using [product_name] [version_no].

Sorry, I see no differences in my full version; both diagrams work the same. Maybe I'll try it later with the demo version, but issues sometimes arise. In the past, main problems were copy-paste errors in LAD, which damaged diagrams. This seems corrected in version [version_no]. [company_name] ought to offer a newer demo version. Regards, [user_name]
The error also appears in the full version of [product_name] [version_no].
Yes, but I think the issue is not with the full version [version_no], but with the absence of a demo version [version_no].

I'm concerned this isn't just a demo version [version_no] issue, but affects the full [product_name] [version_no] too. As stated earlier, the problem doesn't occur in the full version [version_no]. Since the demo is basically a stripped-down full version without online functions, the error likely wouldn't appear in a demo version [version_no]. However, it's doubtful [company_name] will release an updated demo. If you load a program saved in [product_name] [version_no] into [product_name] [version_no], the error disappears.
Thanks [user_name] and [user_name] for your input. The solution is to use an updated demo or to install [product_name] [version_no] which we have ready. Kind regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users report that the [product_name] demo software (version [version_no]) has errors converting between FBD and LAD diagrams, causing inaccurate simulation outcomes. These issues have been fixed in newer, full versions of the software ([version_no]), but the unavailability of an updated demo hampers teaching and learning for educators and students in industrial automation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable conversion between FBD and LAD diagrams in the demo software, ensuring simulations work correctly. They hope the demo version will be updated to reflect the improvements and bug fixes present in recent full versions.
